doc: Service-worker registration and the application-update lifecycle (LCP-034). The host declares which workers exist and vouches for their script URLs; the engine names one and never supplies a URL. A new version of a worker installs and then waits: it takes over only when the engine asks, so update availability and activation are explicit facts and decisions, never something the browser does behind the engine's back. The worker caches a declared shell and serves it when the network fails; it never queues, retries or resolves anything, so synchronisation stays in the engine. Online and offline are the lifecycle pack's facts. Push and background sync are reported as supported or not, and are not enabled by this pack.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: The browser has service workers and this is a secure context.

fields.name: controlled
fields.doc: A worker controls this page, so its requests go through the worker's cache.

fields.name: activeVersion
fields.doc: The version the active worker reports.

fields.name: waitingVersion
fields.doc: A new version that has installed and is waiting for the engine to activate it.

fields.name: push
fields.doc: The Push API exists; nothing here subscribes.

fields.name: backgroundSync
fields.doc: Background Sync exists; nothing here registers a sync.

variants.name: register
variants.doc: Registers the worker the host declared under this name.

variants.name: checkForUpdate
variants.doc: Asks the browser to fetch the worker script again. A changed script installs and then waits; UpdateReady follows.

variants.name: activateUpdate
variants.doc: Tells the waiting worker to take over. ControllerChanged follows; reloading, if the engine wants it, is the engine's navigation.

variants.name: UpdateChecked
variants.doc: The check finished; status says whether a version is installing or waiting.

variants.name: UnknownWorker
variants.doc: The host declared no worker by that name.

variants.name: Failed
variants.doc: The browser refused: the script failed to load or evaluate, the scope was not allowed, or the update check could not reach the server. problem is the browser's error name.

variants.name: UpdateReady
variants.doc: A new version installed while an older one controls the page, and is waiting for activateUpdate.

variants.name: ControllerChanged
variants.doc: A different worker now controls the page (the first activation, or an activated update).

variants.name: UpdateFailed
variants.doc: A new version failed to install and was discarded; the current one keeps control.

types.name: WorkerCommand
types.doc: What the pack posts to a worker. Internal to the pack and its worker; the engine never sees it.
